title: Containers and Kubernetes: could one compromised pod take over the cluster?
short: Make the API server private, enforce Pod Security baseline in every namespace and upgrade within each version's 12 months of patches.
answer: This month, take the API server off the internet, enforce the baseline Pod Security Standard in every namespace and start replacing Ingress NGINX, which has had no security fixes since March 2026[^r136]. Then judge every other setting by whether it stops one compromised pod from reaching its node, the cloud account or a more powerful service account.
audience: Platform, DevOps and security teams running Kubernetes on AKS, EKS, GKE or their own servers, from one cluster to many

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Take the API server off the internet.
items.text: EKS, AKS and GKE expose it by default[^eksendpoint][^aksapi][^gkeharden]. Make it private or admin-only: Microsoft finds exposed APIs, default credentials and unpatched images behind most container compromises[^mddr].

items.title: Enforce Pod Security baseline in every namespace.
items.text: Set the Pod Security Admission label `enforce` to `baseline` to block privileged containers, hostPath and host namespaces[^pss], and `warn` and `audit` to `restricted`[^psa]. North Korea-linked UNC4899 used a privileged pod to break out of its container[^th].

items.title: Treat pod creation as a privileged right.
items.text: Anyone who can create pods in a namespace can mount its Secrets and run as any of its service accounts[^rbacgp]. Each quarter, list who holds that right, `cluster-admin` or the rights below, and cut the list.

items.title: Keep workload credentials short-lived.
items.text: Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` unless a pod calls the API[^appcheck], avoid non-expiring token Secrets[^checklist] and block pods from the node's cloud role[^eksbpiam]. UNC4899 stole database passwords from a pod's environment variables[^th].

items.title: Stay on a supported version, add-ons included.
items.text: Kubernetes patches only its three newest minor versions, for about a year each[^releases]. Ingress NGINX, in about half of cloud native environments, can read every Secret by default and was retired in March 2026[^ingstmt][^ingcve][^r136].

blocks.title: Harden a running cluster in this order

items.title: Who can reach and administer it?
items.text: List each cluster's endpoint, version, add-ons and `cluster-admin` bindings. Find Ingress NGINX with `kubectl get pods -A -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx`[^ingstmt].

items.title: Which pods would Pod Security reject?
items.text: Set the `pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn` and `audit` labels first. They also check Deployments, while `enforce` checks only pods, so a noncompliant Deployment is accepted but its pods are rejected[^psa].

items.title: Does your network plugin enforce NetworkPolicy?
items.text: If not, a NetworkPolicy has no effect[^netpol]. Add default-deny ingress and egress policies to each namespace, then allow what you need, DNS included.

items.title: What does Pod Security miss?
items.text: Add admission rules for image sources and digests[^checklist]; signing is in the supply-chain sheet. ValidatingAdmissionPolicy is built in and can `Warn` and `Audit` before it denies[^vap]; Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper are add-ons[^pss].

items.title: Would you see a takeover?
items.text: Turn on audit logs: they are off by default on EKS[^ekslogs] and need a diagnostic setting on AKS[^aksmon]. Alert on `exec` into pods, new cluster role bindings and Secrets listed by people. Retention is in the logging sheet.

blocks.title: Defaults to change on EKS, AKS and GKE

columns.title: Amazon EKS
items: **Public endpoint.** Enable private access, then limit or disable public access[^eksendpoint].
**aws-auth.** Deprecated: move to access entries and remove the creator's `cluster-admin`[^eksbpiam].
**Support.** 14 months, then 12 of paid extended support, on by default. Extended support for 1.31 ends on 26 November 2026[^eksver].

columns.title: Azure AKS
items: **Public API server.** Use a private cluster or at least authorized IP ranges[^aksapi].
**Local accounts.** On by default and unaudited, they bypass Entra ID. Set `--disable-local-accounts` and rotate certificates[^akslocal].
**Support.** 12 months per version; 1.34 reaches end of life in November 2026[^aksver].

columns.title: Google GKE
items: **Reachable control plane.** Use only the DNS-based endpoint, or authorized networks[^gkeharden].
**Anonymous access.** Only clusters created on 1.35 or later limit it by default; elsewhere set `--anonymous-authentication-config=LIMITED`[^gkeharden].
**Upgrades.** Use a release channel with accelerated patch auto-upgrades[^gkeharden].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Ingress NGINX is archived.** It has had no fixes since 24 March 2026[^r136]. Move to Gateway API or another controller[^ingstmt].
**Kubernetes 1.36 closed old gaps.** It disabled `gitRepo` volumes for good and deprecated Service `externalIPs`[^r136].
**AKS will upgrade unsupported clusters itself.** From 1 June 2027, after a 60-day grace period and regardless of maintenance windows[^akspiu].

**Linux root exploits came with public code.** Three flaws disclosed from 29 April to 13 May 2026 gave local users root on major distributions[^mddr]. Patch node images within the patching sheet's deadlines.

blocks.title: RBAC rights that allow escalation
items: **`get`, `list` or `watch` on Secrets.** List and watch return the contents too[^rbacgp].
**`escalate`, `bind` and `impersonate`.** They bypass RBAC's escalation checks or borrow another user's rights[^rbacgp].
**Any right on `nodes/proxy`.** Even `get` runs commands in every pod on the node, unaudited and past admission control[^rbacgp].
**Webhook, token and volume rights.** Control of webhook configurations, `serviceaccounts/token` or PersistentVolumes exposes admitted objects, mints tokens or mounts the node's disk[^rbacgp].
**`patch` on namespaces.** It lets a user relabel a namespace to a looser Pod Security level[^rbacgp].

blocks.title: Pod and node settings that stop an escape
items: **Non-root, read-only, no escalation.** Restricted requires `runAsNonRoot`, no privilege escalation, seccomp and dropping `ALL` capabilities[^pss]. Add `readOnlyRootFilesystem`[^appcheck].
**User namespaces.** Set `hostUsers: false`, GA since 1.36, to map container root to an unprivileged host user[^userns].
**Minimal images by digest.** Ship no shells or debug tools, pin sha256 digests instead of tags and scan at build and deploy[^checklist].
**Secrets as files.** They leak less than environment variables; mount them from an external store with the Secrets Store CSI Driver[^checklist].
**Kubelet API.** On your own nodes, turn off `--anonymous-auth` and set `--authorization-mode=Webhook`: the defaults allow anonymous access[^kubeletauth].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A service mesh just for encryption.** The checklist suggests one only if your network plugin can't encrypt traffic[^checklist].
**Waiting for fixes to old CVEs.** Scanners can flag CVE-2020-8561, CVE-2020-8562 and CVE-2021-25740 on every version since June 2026; they won't be fixed[^unfixed]. Mitigate once and accept them.
**CPU limits on every pod.** They throttle work and can upset autoscaling; the checklist suggests them only for sensitive workloads[^checklist].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Exempting a controller from Pod Security.** Exempting the ReplicaSet controller exempts everyone who can create a Deployment[^psa].
**Giving CI a cluster-wide service account.** UNC4899 made CI jobs print service account tokens to logs, then used a highly privileged one to escalate[^th]. Scope deploy accounts to namespaces.
**Binding roles to built-in groups.** `system:unauthenticated` is anyone who can reach the API server[^rbacgp]; on GKE, `system:authenticated` includes any Google account[^gkeharden].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Prefer a managed mode with secure defaults: GKE Autopilot disallows privileged pods[^th].
Limit the API server to your VPN or office addresses, and turn on audit logs.
Label every namespace `enforce: baseline` and turn on automatic patch upgrades.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Reach a private API server through a VPN or bastion, with SSO groups mapped to RBAC roles.
Keep admission and network policies in Git, and move each rule from warn to deny.
Upgrade control plane and nodes twice a year, staging cluster first.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Give untrusted tenants their own cluster and each trust level its own namespace[^rbacgp].
On self-managed clusters, load must-have admission policies from disk, beta in 1.37[^r137].
Send audit logs and GuardDuty, Defender for Containers or Falco alerts to the SIEM.
